subproblem.title: Cut-off pull-back test forms agreeing with F^#ω and with F^#(dω) near a compact set
subproblem.statement: For all N, N', k ∈ ℕ, every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) (TestFormOn univ k) and every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N, there are η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) and an open set W ⊇ K such that for every x ∈ W: η(x) = F^#ω(x) := (ω(F(x))).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x), and dη(x) = (dω(F(x))).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x), where d = exteriorDerivative.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' k : ℕ) (F : Euclid N → Euclid N') (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N')) k) (K : Set (Euclid N)), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) F → IsCompact K → ∃ (η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N)) k) (W : Set (Euclid N)), IsOpen W ∧ K ⊆ W ∧ (∀ x ∈ W, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') k) (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)) ∧ ∀ x ∈ W, exteriorDerivative (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid N) k) x = (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') k) (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof 0(e) (cut-offs), 0(h) (smooth pull-back, d(F^#ω) = F^#dω) and A1 (the form ζF^#ω). Notation: P(x) := F^#ω(x) = (ω(F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x); d = exteriorDerivative = extDeriv.
1. Trivial case. If K = ∅ take η := 0 and W := ∅; all claims about x ∈ W are vacuous. Assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Cut-off function. U := Metric.thickening 1 K = {x : infDist x K < 1} is open, bounded (K is compact) and contains K. By IsOpen.exists_contDiff_support_eq there is a C^∞ f : ℝ^N → ℝ with values in [0, 1] and support f = U. f is positive on the nonempty compact K ⊆ U and attains its minimum m > 0 there (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Let W := U ∩ {x : f x > m/2}; W is open and K ⊆ W. Let h(s) := Real.smoothTransition((s − m/4)/(m/4)): h is C^∞, h = 0 on (−∞, m/4], h = 1 on [m/2, ∞) (smoothTransition.one_of_one_le) and 0 ≤ h ≤ 1. Then ζ := h ∘ f is C^∞, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on W, and ζ(x) = h(0) = 0 for x ∉ U. Hence support ζ ⊆ U and tsupport ζ ⊆ closure U, a closed bounded subset of ℝ^N, hence compact.
3. Smoothness of P. The linear map ev : Λ^k(ℝ^N)* → ℝ^{(Fin k → Fin N)}, ev(γ) := (γ(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I k}))_I, is injective (by multilinearity, γ(u_1, …, u_k) = Σ_I γ(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I k})·∏_i (u_i)_{I i}), so it has a linear left inverse ℓ (LinearMap.exists_leftInverse_of_injective), which is continuous because the spaces are finite-dimensional; thus P = ℓ ∘ (ev ∘ P) and it suffices to show that each coordinate x ↦ P(x)(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I k}) = ω(F x)(DF(x)e_{I 1}, …, DF(x)e_{I k}) is C^∞. Expanding again by multilinearity in the standard basis of ℝ^{N'}, this equals Σ_{L : Fin k → Fin N'} ω(F x)(e_{L 1}, …, e_{L k})·∏_i (DF(x) e_{I i})_{L i}, a finite sum of products of C^∞ scalar functions: x ↦ ω(F x)(e_L) is C^∞ (ω C^∞, F C^∞, evaluation continuous linear) and x ↦ (DF(x)e_i)_l is C^∞ (F is C^∞, so x ↦ fderiv ℝ F x is C^∞ by ContDiff.fderiv_right, and L ↦ (L e_i)_l is continuous linear). Hence P is C^∞.
4. Definition of η. η := ζ • P (pointwise scalar multiple). η is C^∞ (product of C^∞ functions), support η ⊆ support ζ, so tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ is compact; hence η ∈ TestFormOn univ k.
5. Values on W. For x ∈ W, ζ(x) = 1, so η(x) = P(x) = F^#ω(x).
6. Exterior derivative on W. Let x ∈ W. Since W is open and η = P on W, η =ᶠ[𝓝 x] P, so dη(x) = dP(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq). By extDeriv_pullback (ω is differentiable at F x since it is C^∞; F is C^∞, hence ContDiffAt ℝ ∞ F x, and minSmoothness ℝ 2 ≤ ∞), dP(x) = (dω(F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x). □
proof_key_steps: C^∞ cut-off ζ with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on an open W ⊇ K and compact support (smooth function with support the 1-thickening of K, composed with a smooth step).
The pull-back P = F^#ω is C^∞ (coordinates on basis tuples are finite sums of products of smooth functions; ev has a continuous linear left inverse).
η := ζ·P is a test form equal to F^#ω on W.
On W, η =ᶠ P, so dη = dP = F^#(dω) by extDeriv_pullback.

subproblem.title: Mollification of Lipschitz maps: C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz approximants within Λ/(j + 1)
subproblem.statement: For all N, N' ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz map F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} there are maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} (j ∈ ℕ), each C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) and Λ-Lipschitz, with |F_j(x) − F(x)| ≤ Λ/(j + 1) for all j ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' : ℕ) (Λ : NNReal) (F : Euclid N → Euclid N'), LipschitzWith Λ F → ∃ Fs : ℕ → Euclid N → Euclid N', (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (Fs j)) ∧ (∀ j, LipschitzWith Λ (Fs j)) ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (x : Euclid N), dist (Fs j x) (F x) ≤ (Λ : ℝ) / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof 0(f) (mollification), with σ := 1/(j + 1).
1. Fix j and σ := 1/(j + 1) > 0. Let b : ℝ^N → ℝ be the C^∞ bump function of a ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn := σ/2 and rOut := σ (instance hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace): b is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, b(0) = 1, support b = ball(0, σ) (ContDiffBump.support_eq), and b has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport).
2. I := ∫ b > 0: b is continuous with compact support, hence integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport); b ≥ 0; its support ball(0, σ) is a nonempty open set and volume on ℝ^N is positive on nonempty open sets (IsOpenPosMeasure of the additive Haar measure), so integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg gives I > 0. Put ϕ := I⁻¹·b: C^∞, ϕ ≥ 0, ∫ϕ = 1, support ϕ ⊆ ball(0, σ), compact support.
3. Define F_j(x) := ∫ ϕ(y)·F(x − y) dy, i.e. F_j = ϕ ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ] F (Mathlib convolution with respect to volume). F is continuous, hence locally integrable, and ϕ is C^∞ with compact support, so F_j is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left). For each x the integrand y ↦ ϕ(y)·F(x − y) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable.
4. Lipschitz bound. For x, x': F_j(x) − F_j(x') = ∫ ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x' − y)) dy, and ‖ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x' − y))‖ ≤ ϕ(y)·Λ‖x − x'‖. Hence ‖F_j(x) − F_j(x')‖ ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·Λ‖x − x'‖ dy = Λ‖x − x'‖ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with the integrable majorant ϕ·Λ‖x − x'‖). So F_j is Λ-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
5. Distance to F. Since ∫ϕ = 1, F_j(x) − F(x) = ∫ ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x)) dy. For y ∈ support ϕ we have ‖y‖ < σ, so ‖ϕ(y)·(F(x − y) − F(x))‖ ≤ ϕ(y)·Λ‖y‖ ≤ ϕ(y)·Λσ; for y ∉ support ϕ the integrand is 0. Hence ‖F_j(x) − F(x)‖ ≤ ∫ ϕ(y)·Λσ dy = Λσ = Λ/(j + 1).
6. Steps 1–5 apply verbatim for every N (for N = 0, ℝ^0 is a point, volume is the unit Dirac mass and ball(0, σ) = {0} is open, nonempty and of positive measure; alternatively F_j := F, which is constant, works). □
proof_key_steps: Normalized C^∞ bump ϕ = b/∫b supported in ball(0, 1/(j+1)) (ContDiffBump; ∫b > 0 by positivity on a nonempty open set).
F_j := ϕ ⋆ F is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
F_j(x) − F_j(x') = ∫ϕ(y)(F(x−y) − F(x'−y)) gives the Lipschitz constant Λ.
F_j(x) − F(x) = ∫ϕ(y)(F(x−y) − F(x)) gives |F_j − F| ≤ Λ/(j+1).

Positivity, integrability, and the zero-dimensional case are justified. The proof establishes the quantified statement without another construction or search obligation.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof 0(a), 0(g) and A2(a), A2(d) (Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.22), stated at the level of forms. Notation. ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{N+1} for t ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^N; Jv := ι(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1; tail y := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp y)). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) = TestFormOn univ k (C^∞ forms with compact support; tsupport ⊆ univ is automatic) and 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k. For a C^∞ map F, F^#ω(x) := (ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x). d = exteriorDerivative (Mathlib extDeriv). 
1. Coordinates. J : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1} is linear and ‖Jv‖ = ‖v‖ (the Euclidean norm of (0, v) is that of v), so J is a continuous linear isometric embedding; ι(t, x) = t·e₀ + Jx; tail is continuous linear with tail(ι(t, x)) = x and y = ι(y 0, tail y). Hence t ↦ ι(t, x) is affine with derivative e₀ and x ↦ ι(t, x) is affine with derivative J.
2. Contraction. For m ∈ ℕ let Φ_m : Λ^{m+1}(ℝ^{N+1})* → Λ^m(ℝ^N)*, Φ_m(γ) := (γ.curryLeft e₀).compContinuousLinearMap J. It is continuous linear (γ ↦ γ.curryLeft is the linear isometry ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI, evaluation at e₀ is continuous linear, and compContinuousLinearMapCLM J is continuous linear), and Φ_m(γ)(v) = γ(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v)) by curryLeft_apply_apply and compContinuousLinearMap_apply.
3. Smoothness of parametric integrals. Claim: if V is a finite-dimensional real normed space and h : ℝ × ℝ^N → V is C^∞, then x ↦ ∫_0^1 h(t, x) dt is C^∞ and has derivative ∫_0^1 D_x h(t, x) dt at x, where D_x h(t, x) := Dh(t, x) ∘ (0, ·) ∈ L(ℝ^N, V). Proof. Fix x₀. (t, x) ↦ D_x h(t, x) is continuous, hence bounded by some B on the compact set [0, 1] × closedBall(x₀, 1); h(t, ·) has derivative D_x h(t, x) at every x; all functions are continuous, hence measurable and interval integrable. By hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le'' (μ = volume, a = 0, b = 1, s = ball(x₀, 1), constant bound B), x ↦ ∫_0^1 h(t, x) dt has derivative ∫_0^1 D_x h(t, x₀) dt at x₀. Now show by induction on n ∈ ℕ, for all finite-dimensional V and all C^∞ h simultaneously, that x ↦ ∫_0^1 h(t, x) dt is C^n: for n = 0 it is differentiable, hence continuous; for n + 1 it is differentiable with derivative x ↦ ∫_0^1 D_x h(t, x) dt, where (t, x) ↦ D_x h(t, x) is C^∞ with values in the finite-dimensional space L(ℝ^N, V) (composition of the C^∞ map Dh with the continuous linear map L ↦ L ∘ (0, ·)), so the derivative is C^n by the induction hypothesis and the function is C^{n+1} (contDiff_succ_iff_hasFDerivAt). Being C^n for every n, it is C^∞.
4. Part (a). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and g(t, x) := Φ_k(ω(ι(t, x))); g is C^∞ (ω is C^∞, (t, x) ↦ t·e₀ + Jx is affine, Φ_k is continuous linear). Put η(x) := ∫_0^1 g(t, x) dt ∈ Λ^k(ℝ^N)*. By step 3, η is C^∞. Evaluation at v is a continuous linear map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply) and commutes with the interval integral of the continuous function g(·, x) (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm), so η(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 g(t, x)(v) dt = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v)) dt, the required formula. Support: let K := {x : ∃ t ∈ [0, 1], ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω}. Since ω has compact support, tsupport ω is compact; K = tail(tsupport ω ∩ {y : y 0 ∈ [0, 1]}) (if ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω with t ∈ [0, 1] then y := ι(t, x) has y 0 = t and tail y = x; conversely y = ι(y 0, tail y)), the continuous image of a compact set, so K is compact and closed. If x ∉ K then ω(ι(t, x)) = 0 for every t ∈ [0, 1], so g(·, x) vanishes on [0, 1] and η(x) = 0. Hence support η ⊆ K and tsupport η ⊆ K. So η is C^∞ with compact support, i.e. an element of TestFormOn univ k, and both conjuncts of (a) hold.
5. Part (b). Let s ∈ ℝ and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}). The affine map a_s(x) := s·e₀ + Jx is proper: ‖a_s(x)‖ ≥ ‖Jx‖ − |s| = ‖x‖ − |s|, so preimages of bounded sets are bounded, and preimages of compact sets are closed and bounded, hence compact. By SimonGMT affinePullbackForm_isTestForm (L := J, b := s·e₀), ρ(x) := (ω(s·e₀ + Jx)).compContinuousLinearMap J is C^∞ with compact support, i.e. ρ ∈ TestFormOn univ k, and ρ(x)(v) = ω(ι(s, x))(J ∘ v).
6. Part (c). Fix β, θ as in (c), x ∈ ℝ^N and v : Fin (k + 1) → ℝ^N. Put w := J ∘ v and W := Fin.cons e₀ w : Fin (k + 2) → ℝ^{N+1}. Let g(t, x') := Φ_k(β(ι(t, x'))) (C^∞ by step 4's argument). By the hypothesis on θ, the evaluation identity of step 4 and ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext, θ(x') = ∫_0^1 g(t, x') dt for every x'.
 (c1) For each t, by extDeriv_apply (β is differentiable): dβ(ι(t, x))(W) = Σ_{i : Fin (k+2)} (−1)^i · D[y ↦ β(y)(i.removeNth W)](ι(t, x))(W i).
 (c2) The term i = 0: removeNth 0 W = Fin.tail W = w (Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons) and W 0 = e₀; by the chain rule along t ↦ ι(t, x) it equals φ'(t) for φ(t) := β(ι(t, x))(w), a C^1 function. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt), ∫_0^1 φ'(t) dt = β(ι(1, x))(w) − β(ι(0, x))(w).
 (c3) The term i = j.succ (j : Fin (k + 1)): W (j.succ) = w j = J(v j), and removeNth j.succ W = Fin.cons e₀ (removeNth j w) = Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ removeNth j v) (both sides agree at 0 and at every successor index, since Fin.removeNth p i = p ∘ i.succAbove, j.succ.succAbove 0 = 0 and j.succ.succAbove l.succ = (j.succAbove l).succ). By the chain rule along x' ↦ ι(t, x') (derivative J), with u := removeNth j v: D[y ↦ β(y)(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ u))](ι(t, x))(J v_j) = D[x' ↦ β(ι(t, x'))(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ u))](x)(v_j) = D[x' ↦ g(t, x')(u)](x)(v_j).
 (c4) By step 3 (derivative of a parametric integral) composed with the evaluation map at u (continuous linear), D[x' ↦ θ(x')(u)](x) = ∫_0^1 D[x' ↦ g(t, x')(u)](x) dt for every u. By extDeriv_apply for the smooth form θ, dθ(x)(v) = Σ_{j : Fin (k+1)} (−1)^j D[x' ↦ θ(x')(removeNth j v)](x)(v_j) = ∫_0^1 Σ_j (−1)^j D[x' ↦ g(t, x')(removeNth j v)](x)(v_j) dt.
 (c5) Every term in (c1) is continuous in t (β is C^∞), hence interval integrable. Integrating (c1) over [0, 1], using (c2), (c3), (c4) and (−1)^{j.succ} = −(−1)^j: ∫_0^1 dβ(ι(t, x))(W) dt = β(ι(1, x))(w) − β(ι(0, x))(w) − dθ(x)(v). This is (c).
7. Part (d). For β ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N+1}), x and v : Fin 0 → ℝ^N: by extDeriv_apply with n = 0 the only index is 0, removeNth 0 (Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v)) = J ∘ v (both are the empty tuple), so dβ(ι(t, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v)) = D[y ↦ β(y)(J ∘ v)](ι(t, x))(e₀) = d/dt[β(ι(t, x))(J ∘ v)]. The fundamental theorem of calculus gives (d).
8. Part (e). Let κ : Λ^k(ℝ^N)* → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k → Fin N), κ(γ) I := if StrictMono I then γ(fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ (I i)) else 0; κ is continuous linear. By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and (if p then a else 0)^2 = (if p then a^2 else 0), ‖κ(γ)‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm γ for every γ. t ↦ κ(f(t)) is continuous, hence interval integrable. For each I, using the hypothesis with v := (e_{I i})_i and that the coordinate projection is continuous linear (so it commutes with the interval integral): κ(α) I = [StrictMono I]·∫_0^1 f(t)(e_I) dt = ∫_0^1 κ(f(t)) I dt = (∫_0^1 κ(f(t)) dt) I. Hence κ(α) = ∫_0^1 κ(f(t)) dt, and by intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const (for t ∈ Ι 0 1 ⊆ [0, 1], ‖κ(f(t))‖ = |f(t)| ≤ c): |α| = ‖κ(α)‖ ≤ c·|1 − 0| = c. □
proof_key_steps: J is a linear isometric embedding, ι(t, x) = t·e₀ + Jx, tail(ι(t, x)) = x; the contraction Φ(γ) = (γ.curryLeft e₀) ∘ J is continuous linear with Φ(γ)(v) = γ(e₀, Jv).
Parametric integrals x ↦ ∫_0^1 h(t, x) dt of C^∞ h are C^∞ with derivative ∫_0^1 D_x h dt (dominated differentiation under the interval integral, induction on the order).
(a) η(x) := ∫_0^1 Φ(ω(ι(t, x))) dt is C^∞, satisfies the evaluation formula, and vanishes off the compact set tail(tsupport ω ∩ {y_0 ∈ [0, 1]}).
(b) ρ is the affine pull-back of ω by the proper map x ↦ s·e₀ + Jx (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm_isTestForm).

(c) Expand dβ(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) by extDeriv_apply: the 0-th term is ∂_t[β(ι(t, x))(Jv)], the others are −d_x of the slice integrand; integrate (FTC, differentiation under the integral) to get S_{dβ} = i_1^#β − i_0^#β − dθ.
(d) In degree 0 only the ∂_t term occurs; integrate by the FTC.
(e) The coefficient map κ is continuous linear with ‖κ(γ)‖ = |γ|; κ(α) = ∫_0^1 κ(f(t)) dt, so |α| ≤ ∫_0^1 |f(t)| dt ≤ c.

The coordinate calculation proves the correct boundary sign, including degree zero, and the coefficient map proves the integral norm bound. No circular reliance occurs.

subproblem.statement: Assume (VO), the vanishing-off-support antecedent: for all P, n, U, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0; and (REP), the mass-representation antecedent: for U open and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U there are a measure μ (μ(Uᶜ) = 0, finite on compact subsets of U) and ξ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n (μ-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α) with M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W, T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ for all ω, and, if also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U, μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 (the exact frozen Lean types, written as antecedents). Then for all N, k ∈ ℕ: (MSB) if X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) has M(X) < ∞, ψ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N), c ∈ ℝ and |ψ(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ spt X, then |X(ψ)| ≤ c·M(X) (M(X) as a real number via ENNReal.toReal); (BC) if T₀ : 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) → ℝ is linear, C ∈ ℝ, and |T₀(ω)| ≤ C·c whenever c ∈ ℝ and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, then there is T ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with T(ω) = T₀(ω) for all ω and M(T) ≤ ofReal C; (SB) spt ∂X ⊆ spt X for every X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^N); (LOC) if X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N), W ⊆ ℝ^N is open, spt X ⊆ W, and η, η' ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) satisfy η(x) = η'(x) for all x ∈ W, then X(η) = X(η').

Source: parent proof A0 (representation of finite-mass currents via (REP) and (VO)), 0(b) (bounded linear functionals are currents with mass ≤ C) and 0(c) (S2), (S3). Conventions: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sSup {ofReal(T ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^k, tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 ∀x} and M(T) = T.mass = M_univ(T). spt T = univ ∖ zeroRegion T, where zeroRegion T is the union of the open sets W with compact closure (⊆ univ) on which T vanishes (T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W); zeroRegion T is open.
1. (SB). Let X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^N) and x ∉ spt X. Then x ∈ zeroRegion X: there is an open W ∋ x with compact closure on which X vanishes. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k with tsupport ω ⊆ W we have ∂X(ω) = X(dω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply) and tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂X(ω) = 0. Thus ∂X vanishes on W, W is one of the sets in the union defining zeroRegion ∂X, and x ∉ spt ∂X.
2. (LOC). ψ := η − η' vanishes on the open set W, so support ψ ⊆ Wᶜ, which is closed; hence tsupport ψ ⊆ Wᶜ, which is disjoint from spt X ⊆ W. By (VO) (P := N, n := k, U := univ), X(ψ) = 0, i.e. X(η) = X(η') by linearity of X.
3. (MSB), representation. Let X with M(X) < ∞. For every W, M_W(X) ≤ M(X) < ∞ (massOn_mono, W ⊆ univ); in particular the hypothesis of (REP) holds for U := univ (open). (REP) gives μ, ξ with: M_W(X) = μ(W) for every open W; ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α; X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k.
4. (MSB), total mass. μ(univ) = M_univ(X) = M(X) < ∞ (univ is open), so μ is a finite measure and μ(univ).toReal = M(X).toReal.
5. (MSB), concentration. Z := (spt X)ᶜ = zeroRegion X is open, so μ(Z) = M_Z(X). Every ω admissible for M_Z(X) has tsupport ω ⊆ Z, i.e. disjoint from spt X, so X(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence each element of the defining set is ofReal 0 = 0 and M_Z(X) = 0. So μ(Z) = 0 and μ-a.e. x lies in spt X.
6. (MSB), estimate. For μ-a.e. x (namely x ∈ spt X): |ξ(x)(ψ(x))| ≤ |ψ(x)| ≤ c. By norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const (finite measure, a.e. bound c; no sign condition on c is needed): |X(ψ)| = |∫ ξ(x)(ψ(x)) dμ| ≤ c·μ.real(univ) = c·M(X).toReal.
7. (BC), coefficient bound. Let A := sqrt(N^k). For a k-covector α, each coefficient satisfies |α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I k})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖e_{I i}‖ = ‖α‖ (operator-norm bound for continuous multilinear maps), and there are at most N^k index tuples, so |α| ≤ A·‖α‖.
8. (BC), sign of C. Applying the hypothesis to ω = 0 and c = 1 gives 0 ≤ C.
9. (BC), continuity. Let (ω_j) satisfy TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0: there is a compact K ⊆ univ containing every tsupport ω_j such that, in particular, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j → 0 uniformly on K. Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every ε > 0 there is j₀ with ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ K; for x ∉ K, ω_j(x) = 0. So for j ≥ j₀, |ω_j(x)| ≤ A·ε for every x and |T₀(ω_j)| ≤ C·A·ε. Hence T₀(ω_j) → 0, so T := ⟨T₀, this continuity⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn univ k with T(ω) = T₀(ω) for every ω.
10. (BC), mass. For every ω admissible for M_univ (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x): T(ω) ≤ |T₀(ω)| ≤ C·1, so ofReal(T ω) ≤ ofReal C. Taking the supremum, M(T) ≤ ofReal C. □

(LOC): tsupport(η − η') ⊆ Wᶜ is disjoint from spt X, so (VO) gives X(η − η') = 0.
(MSB): (REP) with U = univ gives μ, ξ; μ(univ) = M(X), μ((spt X)ᶜ) = M_{(spt X)ᶜ}(X) = 0 by (VO); |∫ ξ(ψ) dμ| ≤ c·μ(univ).
(BC): |α| ≤ sqrt(N^k)‖α‖, so test-form convergence to 0 forces T₀(ω_j) → 0; admissible forms give M(T) ≤ ofReal C.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof A2 (product [[0,1]] × X via the slice operator, its support, boundary formula and mass, A2(a)–(f)) and the verification of conjuncts (7)–(9). Notation: ι, J, e₀ as in the statement; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; NC as in the parent. Siblings used: Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_forms ((a) slices, (b) affine slices, (c), (d) homotopy identities, (e) Minkowski bound) and Submission.cmcdt_lpo_current_toolkit applied to (VO), (REP) ((MSB), (BC), (SB), (LOC)). (L1), (L2) are the first two conjuncts of (LB). Φ(γ) := (γ.curryLeft e₀).compContinuousLinearMap J for a (m+1)-covector γ on ℝ^{N+1}; Φ(γ)(v) = γ(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v)), Φ is continuous linear, and ‖J‖ ≤ 1 (‖Jv‖ = ‖v‖), ‖e₀‖ = 1.
1. Pointwise bounds. For a (m+1)-covector γ: |Φ(γ)| ≤ ‖J‖^m·|γ.curryLeft e₀| ≤ ‖e₀‖·|γ| = |γ| by (L1), (L2). For an m-covector γ: |γ.compContinuousLinearMap J| ≤ ‖J‖^m·|γ| ≤ |γ| by (L1).
2. Slice operator. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) let S_ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) be the test form of slice (a) (by choice). Any test form with the slice formula equals S_ω (test forms are determined by their values; ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext). Hence ω ↦ S_ω is linear: S_{ω₁} + S_{ω₂} and c·S_ω satisfy the slice formulas of ω₁ + ω₂ and c·ω (interval integrals of continuous integrands are additive and homogeneous). Bound: if |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y then |S_ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, by slice (e) with f(t) := Φ(ω(ι(t, x))) (continuous; S_ω(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 f(t)(v) dt; |f(t)| ≤ |ω(ι(t, x))| ≤ c by step 1). The same holds in every degree.
3. Definition. If M(X) < ∞, T₀^X(ω) := X(S_ω) is linear in ω (step 2) and |T₀^X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X).toReal whenever |ω| ≤ c (step 2 and (MSB) with the bound c on all of ℝ^N). By (BC) there is a current cyl(X) ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with cyl(X)(ω) = X(S_ω) for all ω and M(cyl X) ≤ ofReal(M(X).toReal) = M(X). If M(X) = ∞ put cyl(X) := 0.
4. Conjunct (9). For NC X and ω, η := S_ω satisfies the formula and cyl(X)(ω) = X(S_ω) = X(η).
5. Conjunct (8). For NC X, Y, M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y) < ∞ (for admissible ω, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) + Y(−ω) and −ω is admissible), so cyl(X − Y)(ω) = (X − Y)(S_ω) = X(S_ω) − Y(S_ω) = cyl(X)(ω) − cyl(Y)(ω) for every ω; GeometricCurrentOn.ext.
6. Conjunct (7), mass: M(cyl X) ≤ M(X) < ∞ by step 3.
7. Conjunct (7), support and compactness. C := {ι(t, x) : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt X} is compact (continuous image of [0, 1] × spt X). Let y ∉ C, r := infDist y C > 0 (r := 1 if C = ∅) and B := ball(y, r/2) (open, compact closure). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with tsupport ω ⊆ B. By slice (a), tsupport S_ω ⊆ K_ω := {x : ∃ t ∈ [0, 1], ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω}, and K_ω ∩ spt X = ∅ (if x ∈ spt X and ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω ⊆ B with t ∈ [0, 1], then ι(t, x) ∈ C and dist(ι(t, x), y) < r/2 < r, impossible). So S_ω = 0 on the open set (tsupport S_ω)ᶜ ⊇ spt X, and X(S_ω) = X(0) = 0 by (LOC). Hence cyl(X) vanishes on B, y ∈ zeroRegion(cyl X), y ∉ spt cyl(X). Therefore spt cyl(X) ⊆ C, which is the set in (7); spt cyl(X) is closed (complement of the open zero region), hence compact as a closed subset of C.
8. Conjunct (7), boundary mass. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}) with |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y. ∂cyl(X)(ω) = cyl(X)(dω) = X(S_{dω}). Let ρ₁, ρ₀ be the test forms of slice (b) for ω and s = 1, 0; ρ_s(x) = (ω(ι(s, x))).compContinuousLinearMap J, so |ρ_s(x)| ≤ c by step 1. Case k = 0: by slice (d), S_{dω}(x)(v) = ω(ι(1, x))(J ∘ v) − ω(ι(0, x))(J ∘ v), so S_{dω} = ρ₁ − ρ₀ and |∂cyl(X)(ω)| ≤ |X(ρ₁)| + |X(ρ₀)| ≤ 2c·M(X).toReal by (MSB). Case k = k' + 1: θ := S_ω ∈ 𝒟^{k'}(ℝ^N) satisfies the hypothesis of slice (c) for β := ω, so S_{dω} = ρ₁ − ρ₀ − dθ, and ∂cyl(X)(ω) = X(ρ₁) − X(ρ₀) − ∂X(θ). |θ(x)| ≤ c by step 2 and M(∂X) = boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞, so (MSB) for X and ∂X gives |∂cyl(X)(ω)| ≤ c·(2·M(X).toReal + (boundaryMassOn X univ).toReal). For admissible ω (c = 1) this gives ofReal(∂cyl(X)(ω)) ≤ ofReal(2·M(X).toReal + (boundaryMassOn X univ).toReal); taking the supremum, M(∂ cyl X) < ∞. □

Let lpush_{N,N',k} : (ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}) and cyl_{N,k} : 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) → 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) be arbitrary families (currents on univ) satisfying (PA) for all N, N', k ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, Λ' ∈ ℝ, every Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, every X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞, every sequence of C^∞ maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} with ‖DF_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ' for all j and x ∈ spt X and F_j → F uniformly on spt X (TendstoUniformlyOn), every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) and every sequence η_j ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) such that each η_j equals F_j^#ω on some open set containing spt X: X(η_j) → lpush(F, X)(ω); the parent's conjunct (7) for cyl (for X with compact support, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞: spt cyl(X) compact, M(cyl X) < ∞, M(∂ cyl X) < ∞, spt cyl(X) ⊆ {ι(t, x) : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt X}); and the parent's conjunct (9) for cyl (for such X and ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) there is η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with η(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) dt for all x, v and cyl(X)(ω) = X(η)). Then the parent's conjuncts (10), (11), (12) hold verbatim: for Λ, L ∈ ℝ≥0, Λ-Lipschitz F, G : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, L-Lipschitz H : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'} with H(ι(t, x)) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) for x ∈ spt X, t ∈ [0, 1]: (10) lpush(G, X) − lpush(F, X) = ∂ lpush(H, cyl X) for X ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^N) with compact support and finite mass; (11) lpush(G, X) − lpush(F, X) − lpush(H, cyl ∂X) = ∂ lpush(H, cyl X) for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^N) with compact support, M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞; (12) M(lpush(H, cyl X)) ≤ ofReal δ·(2Λ)^k·M(X) for X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support, M(X) < ∞, boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ and δ ∈ ℝ with |F(x) − G(x)| ≤ δ for x ∈ spt X.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof A3 (smooth homotopy formula at the level of test forms) and A4(f) (Lipschitz homotopy formula and its mass bound), with the limit taken through the approximation hypothesis (PA) instead of weak convergence and lower semicontinuity. Notation. ι(t, x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)), Jv := ι(0, v), e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1, tail y := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp y)); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; F^#ω(x) := (ω(F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x); Φ(γ) := (γ.curryLeft e₀).compContinuousLinearMap J (continuous linear, Φ(γ)(v) = γ(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v))). NC X: compact support, M(X) < ∞, boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞. Siblings used: Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_forms ((b) affine slices, (c), (d) homotopy identities, (e) Minkowski bound), Submission.cmcdt_lpo_cutoff_pullback (CP), Submission.cmcdt_lpo_mollify_lipschitz (Mo), Submission.cmcdt_lpo_current_toolkit applied to (VO), (REP) ((MSB), (SB), (LOC)). (L1), (L2) are the first two conjuncts of (LB). Test forms with equal values are equal (Subtype.ext, funext, ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext).
1. Facts on X. In (10), X ∈ 𝒟_0 with compact support and M(X) < ∞ is NC (boundaryMassOn in degree 0 is 0). In (11), X is NC and ∂X ∈ 𝒟_k is NC: spt ∂X ⊆ spt X by (SB), a closed subset of a compact set; M(∂X) < ∞; boundaryMassOn ∂X univ = 0 (degree 0 by definition, otherwise ∂∂X = 0). In (12), X is NC. In all cases (7) applies to X (and to ∂X in (11)): cyl(X) is NC and spt cyl(X) ⊆ C := {ι(t, x) : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt X}, which is compact; in (11) also spt cyl(∂X) ⊆ {ι(t, x) : t ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ spt ∂X} ⊆ C.
2. Smooth approximations. Let F_j := Mo(F, Λ), G_j := Mo(G, Λ): C^∞, Λ-Lipschitz (so ‖DF_j‖, ‖DG_j‖ ≤ Λ by norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), ‖F_j − F‖, ‖G_j − G‖ ≤ Λσ_j with σ_j := 1/(j + 1). Define H_j(y) := F_j(tail y) + (y 0)·(G_j(tail y) − F_j(tail y)). Then: (a) H_j is C^∞, H_j(ι(t, x)) = F_j(x) + t(G_j(x) − F_j(x)) for all t, x, H_j ∘ ι(1, ·) = G_j and H_j ∘ ι(0, ·) = F_j. (b) At y = ι(t, x): DH_j(y)e₀ = G_j(x) − F_j(x) and DH_j(y) ∘ J = DF_j(x) + t(DG_j(x) − DF_j(x)) =: A_t^j(x), with ‖A_t^j(x)‖ ≤ (1 − t)Λ + tΛ = Λ for t ∈ [0, 1]; and for every w, DH_j(y)w = DF_j(x)(tail w) + (w 0)(G_j(x) − F_j(x)) + t(DG_j(x) − DF_j(x))(tail w), so ‖DH_j(y)‖ ≤ 3Λ + ‖G_j(x) − F_j(x)‖ for t ∈ [0, 1]. (c) ‖G_j(x) − F_j(x)‖ ≤ ‖G(x) − F(x)‖ + 2Λσ_j for all x; with D := sup_{x ∈ spt X} ‖G(x) − F(x)‖ (finite by compactness; 0 if spt X = ∅), ‖DH_j(y)‖ ≤ Λ' := 5Λ + D for all j and y ∈ C. (d) For y = ι(t, x) ∈ C: H_j(y) − H(y) = (1 − t)(F_j(x) − F(x)) + t(G_j(x) − G(x)) by the hypothesis on H, so ‖H_j(y) − H(y)‖ ≤ Λσ_j; hence H_j → H uniformly on C, and on every subset of C.
3. Cut-off pull-backs and end slices. Fix a degree m and ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^{N'}). By CP for H_j, ω and the compact C there are β_j ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^{N+1}) and open W_j ⊇ C with β_j = H_j^#ω and dβ_j = (dω(H_j ·)).compContinuousLinearMap (DH_j ·) on W_j. By slice (b) there are ρ_{1,j}, ρ_{0,j} ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^N) with ρ_{s,j}(x)(v) = β_j(ι(s, x))(J ∘ v). V_j := {x : ι(0, x) ∈ W_j ∧ ι(1, x) ∈ W_j} is open and contains spt X, and for x ∈ V_j, by (a) and the chain rule (D(H_j ∘ ι(1, ·))(x) = DH_j(ι(1, x)) ∘ J): ρ_{1,j}(x) = (ω(G_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (DG_j x) = G_j^#ω(x) and ρ_{0,j}(x) = F_j^#ω(x). Hence, if X is NC of degree m, (PA) (maps ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, approximants G_j resp. F_j with derivative bound Λ, uniformly convergent on ℝ^N) gives X(ρ_{1,j}) → lpush(G, X)(ω) and X(ρ_{0,j}) → lpush(F, X)(ω). Moreover, (PA) for maps ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'} applies to H (L-Lipschitz) with approximants H_j (C^∞, ‖DH_j‖ ≤ Λ' on C, H_j → H uniformly on C) and any NC current Y ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^{N+1}) with spt Y ⊆ C: Y(β_j) → lpush(H, Y)(ω), and, for the form dω, Y'(dβ_j) → lpush(H, Y')(dω) for NC Y' ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with spt Y' ⊆ C (dβ_j = H_j^#(dω) on W_j ⊇ C).
4. Conjunct (10). X ∈ 𝒟_0, m := 0, ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N'}). By step 3 with Y' := cyl(X) (NC, spt ⊆ C): cyl(X)(dβ_j) → lpush(H, cyl X)(dω) = ∂ lpush(H, cyl X)(ω). By (9) for X and dβ_j, cyl(X)(dβ_j) = X(η_j) with η_j(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 dβ_j(ι(t, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v)) dt; by slice (d) for β_j, η_j(x)(v) = β_j(ι(1, x))(J ∘ v) − β_j(ι(0, x))(J ∘ v), so η_j = ρ_{1,j} − ρ_{0,j} and cyl(X)(dβ_j) = X(ρ_{1,j}) − X(ρ_{0,j}) → lpush(G, X)(ω) − lpush(F, X)(ω). By uniqueness of limits the two currents agree on ω; GeometricCurrentOn.ext gives (10).
5. Conjunct (11). X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}, m := k + 1, ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}). By step 3: cyl(X)(dβ_j) → ∂ lpush(H, cyl X)(ω) (Y' := cyl(X)), and cyl(∂X)(β_j) → lpush(H, cyl ∂X)(ω) (Y := cyl(∂X), NC with spt ⊆ C). By (9) for X and dβ_j: cyl(X)(dβ_j) = X(η_j), η_j the slice of dβ_j. By (9) for ∂X and β_j: cyl(∂X)(β_j) = ∂X(θ_j) = X(dθ_j), θ_j ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) the slice of β_j. By slice (c) for β_j and θ_j: η_j = ρ_{1,j} − ρ_{0,j} − dθ_j. Hence cyl(X)(dβ_j) = X(ρ_{1,j}) − X(ρ_{0,j}) − cyl(∂X)(β_j), and letting j → ∞: ∂ lpush(H, cyl X)(ω) = lpush(G, X)(ω) − lpush(F, X)(ω) − lpush(H, cyl ∂X)(ω). Ext gives (11).
6. Conjunct (12), empty support. If spt X = ∅ then X = 0 by (VO); for every test form ω' on ℝ^{N+1}, (9) gives cyl(X)(ω') = X(η) = 0. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}), step 3 with Y := cyl(X) gives lpush(H, cyl X)(ω) = lim cyl(X)(β_j) = 0. So lpush(H, cyl X) = 0, its mass is 0, and (12) holds.
7. Conjunct (12), nonempty support. Then δ ≥ 0 (evaluate the hypothesis at a point of spt X) and Λ ≥ 0. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}) be admissible (|ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y). By step 3 with Y := cyl(X): cyl(X)(β_j) → lpush(H, cyl X)(ω), and by (9) cyl(X)(β_j) = X(θ_j), θ_j the slice of β_j. Fix x ∈ spt X; for t ∈ [0, 1], ι(t, x) ∈ C ⊆ W_j, so β_j(ι(t, x)) = (ω(p)).compContinuousLinearMap (DH_j(ι(t, x))) with p := H_j(ι(t, x)), and f_j(t) := Φ(β_j(ι(t, x))) (continuous, θ_j(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 f_j(t)(v) dt) equals ((ω(p)).curryLeft (G_j x − F_j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (A_t^j(x)) by step 2(b). By (L1), (L2) and step 2(c): |f_j(t)| ≤ Λ^k·‖G_j x − F_j x‖·|ω(p)| ≤ Λ^k(δ + 2Λσ_j). By slice (e), |θ_j(x)| ≤ Λ^k(δ + 2Λσ_j) for x ∈ spt X, and by (MSB) |X(θ_j)| ≤ Λ^k(δ + 2Λσ_j)·M(X).toReal. Letting j → ∞: |lpush(H, cyl X)(ω)| ≤ Λ^k·δ·M(X).toReal ≤ (2Λ)^k·δ·M(X).toReal. Hence ofReal(lpush(H, cyl X)(ω)) ≤ ofReal((2Λ)^k·δ·M(X).toReal) = ofReal δ·(2Λ)^k·M(X) (δ ≥ 0, Λ ≥ 0, M(X) < ∞), and taking the supremum over admissible ω gives (12). □
proof_key_steps: Normality bookkeeping: X, ∂X and cyl(X), cyl(∂X) are NC with supports in C = ι([0,1] × spt X) (SB, (7)).
Mollify F, G (Mo) and interpolate H_j := F_j∘tail + y_0(G_j − F_j)∘tail: C^∞, derivative bounded on C, H_j → H uniformly on C, H_j∘ι(1,·) = G_j, H_j∘ι(0,·) = F_j.
Cut off H_j^#ω near C (CP); end slices ρ_{s,j} equal G_j^#ω, F_j^#ω near spt X; (PA) turns X(ρ_{1,j}), X(ρ_{0,j}), cyl(·)(β_j), cyl(·)(dβ_j) into lpush values.
(10), (11): (9) plus the slice homotopy identities (d), (c) give cyl(X)(dβ_j) = X(ρ_{1,j}) − X(ρ_{0,j}) [− cyl(∂X)(β_j)]; pass to the limit and use ext.
(12): |Φ(β_j(ι(t, x)))| ≤ Λ^k(δ + 2Λσ_j) on spt X by (L1), (L2); Minkowski bound and (MSB), limit, and Λ^k ≤ (2Λ)^k; the empty-support case gives the zero current.

audit.reason: PA, (7) and (9) suffice for arbitrary operator families, so no dependency on their implementations is missing. The smooth interpolants have uniformly bounded derivatives on the required supports and converge there to H. Passing the slice identities and evaluation bounds through PA proves exactly (10)–(12), including empty support and negative displacement bounds.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof A1 (smooth push-forward X(ζF^#ω)), A4(a)–(e) (Lipschitz push-forward as a limit of mollified push-forwards, its mass, boundary, support, locality and linearity) and the verification of conjuncts (1)–(6); the approximation property (PA) is the A4(c)/(e) argument applied to arbitrary smooth approximants. Notation: NC X means IsCompact X.support, X.mass < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; F^#ω(x) := (ω(F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x). Siblings used: Submission.cmcdt_lpo_cutoff_pullback (CP), Submission.cmcdt_lpo_mollify_lipschitz (Mo), Submission.cmcdt_lpo_current_toolkit applied to (VO), (REP) ((MSB), (BC), (SB), (LOC)), and Submission.cmcdt_lpo_smooth_homotopy_estimate applied to (VO), (REP), (LB) (E). (L1) is the first conjunct of (LB).
1. Preliminaries. (i) Every test form ω satisfies a(ω) := sup_y |ω(y)| < ∞ and b(ω) := sup_y |dω(y)| < ∞ (covectorEuclideanNorm is continuous, being the square root of a polynomial in finitely many continuous evaluations, and ω, dω are continuous with compact support). (ii) If spt X = ∅ then X = 0 by (VO). (iii) NC is closed under differences: for NC X, Y, zeroRegion X ∩ zeroRegion Y ⊆ zeroRegion(X − Y) (intersect the two neighbourhoods), so spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y is a closed subset of a compact set; M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y) because for admissible ω, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) + Y(−ω) and −ω is admissible (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg); ∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y (ext), so likewise boundaryMassOn (X − Y) univ ≤ boundaryMassOn X univ + boundaryMassOn Y univ (trivial in degree 0). (iv) If X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} is NC then ∂X is NC: spt ∂X ⊆ spt X (SB) is closed in a compact set, M(∂X) < ∞, and boundaryMassOn ∂X univ = 0 (degree 0 by definition; otherwise ∂∂X = 0 by GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary and the zero current has mass 0). (v) A C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz map has ‖DF(x)‖ ≤ Λ everywhere (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
2. Comparison estimate. Let X be NC of degree k, ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}), F', G' C^∞ with ‖DF'(x)‖, ‖DG'(x)‖ ≤ Λ'' on spt X, and η', η'' test forms equal to F'^#ω, G'^#ω on open sets containing spt X. Put δ := sup_{x ∈ spt X} ‖F'(x) − G'(x)‖ (finite by compactness; δ := 0 if spt X = ∅) and C_X(Λ'', ω) := Λ''^k·M(X).toReal·b(ω) + Λ''^{k−1}·(boundaryMassOn X univ).toReal·a(ω). Then (E) gives |X(η'') − X(η')| ≤ δ·C_X(Λ'', ω).
3. Definition. Let N, N', k, F, X be given. If F is Lipschitz (∃ Λ₀, LipschitzWith Λ₀ F) and X is NC, choose such a Λ₀ and let F_i := Mo(F, Λ₀) (C^∞, Λ₀-Lipschitz, ‖F_i − F‖ ≤ Λ₀/(i + 1)), so ‖DF_i‖ ≤ Λ₀ by (v). For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) let η_i^ω be the test form given by CP for F_i, ω and the compact set spt X (equal to F_i^#ω on an open set containing spt X). (A) (X(η_i^ω))_i is Cauchy: by step 2 with F' := F_i, G' := F_l, Λ'' := Λ₀ and δ ≤ Λ₀(1/(i + 1) + 1/(l + 1)), |X(η_l^ω) − X(η_i^ω)| ≤ Λ₀(1/(i + 1) + 1/(l + 1))·C_X(Λ₀, ω) → 0. Let T₀(ω) := lim_i X(η_i^ω) (ℝ is complete). (B) T₀ is linear: η_i^{ω₁} + η_i^{ω₂} equals F_i^#(ω₁ + ω₂) on the intersection of the two open sets (compContinuousLinearMap is additive in the covector), so by (LOC) X(η_i^{ω₁+ω₂}) = X(η_i^{ω₁}) + X(η_i^{ω₂}); similarly X(η_i^{cω}) = c·X(η_i^ω); pass to the limit. (C) T₀ is bounded: if |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y, then for x ∈ spt X, |η_i^ω(x)| = |(ω(F_i x)).compContinuousLinearMap (DF_i x)| ≤ ‖DF_i(x)‖^k·|ω(F_i x)| ≤ Λ₀^k·c by (L1), so |X(η_i^ω)| ≤ Λ₀^k·c·M(X).toReal by (MSB) and |T₀(ω)| ≤ (Λ₀^k·M(X).toReal)·c. By (BC) there is a current, defined to be lpush(F, X), with lpush(F, X)(ω) = T₀(ω) for all ω. In all other cases put lpush(F, X) := 0.
4. (PA). Let F be Λ-Lipschitz, X NC, F_j' := the given C^∞ maps with ‖DF_j'‖ ≤ Λ' on spt X and F_j' → F uniformly on spt X, ω and η_j as in (PA). F is Lipschitz, so lpush(F, X)(ω) = lim_i X(η_i^ω) with F_i, Λ₀ from step 3. If spt X = ∅ then X = 0, every X(η_j) is 0 and lpush(F, X)(ω) = lim 0 = 0. Otherwise let Λ'' := max(Λ₀, Λ') and ε_j := sup_{x ∈ spt X}‖F_j'(x) − F(x)‖ (finite for large j, → 0 by uniform convergence). By step 2 (F' := F_i, G' := F_j'), |X(η_j) − X(η_i^ω)| ≤ (ε_j + Λ₀/(i + 1))·C_X(Λ'', ω). Letting i → ∞: |X(η_j) − lpush(F, X)(ω)| ≤ ε_j·C_X(Λ'', ω) → 0. Hence X(η_j) → lpush(F, X)(ω).
5. Conjunct (1). id is 1-Lipschitz; take F_j' := id (C^∞, ‖D id‖ ≤ 1, trivially uniformly convergent) and η_j := ω, which equals id^#ω = (ω x).compContinuousLinearMap (ContinuousLinearMap.id) = ω(x) everywhere (fderiv of id is id). By (PA), lpush(id, X)(ω) = lim X(ω) = X(ω) for every ω; GeometricCurrentOn.ext.
6. Conjunct (2). X − Y is NC by (iii). Let F_i := Mo(F, Λ) and η_i := CP(F_i, ω, spt X ∪ spt Y) (compact). η_i equals F_i^#ω on an open set containing spt X, spt Y and spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, and F_i → F uniformly. By (PA) for X, Y and X − Y: lpush(F, X − Y)(ω) = lim (X − Y)(η_i) = lim X(η_i) − lim Y(η_i) = lpush(F, X)(ω) − lpush(F, Y)(ω); ext.
7. Conjunct (3). Let F_i := Mo(F, Λ) and η_i := CP(F_i, ω, spt X). F_i → F uniformly on ℝ^N, hence F_i → G uniformly on spt X (F = G there). By (PA) for F and for G (both Λ-Lipschitz), lpush(F, X)(ω) and lpush(G, X)(ω) are both lim X(η_i); ext.
8. Conjunct (4), mass. With F_i := Mo(F, Λ) and η_i := CP(F_i, ω, spt X), for admissible ω (|ω| ≤ 1): |X(η_i)| ≤ Λ^k·M(X).toReal by (L1) and (MSB) as in step 3(C); by (PA), |lpush(F, X)(ω)| ≤ Λ^k·M(X).toReal, so ofReal(lpush(F, X)(ω)) ≤ ofReal(Λ^k·M(X).toReal) = (Λ : ℝ≥0∞)^k·M(X) (M(X) < ∞). Taking the supremum, M(lpush(F, X)) ≤ Λ^k·M(X).
9. Conjunct (4), support. If spt X = ∅ then X = 0 and lpush(F, X)(ω) = 0 for every ω by (PA), so lpush(F, X) = 0, whose zero region is everything and support empty. Otherwise let y ∉ F(spt X); F(spt X) is compact, so r := infDist y (F(spt X)) > 0. Let B := ball(y, r/3) (open, compact closure). Let ω have tsupport ω ⊆ B, F_i := Mo(F, Λ), η_i := CP(F_i, ω, spt X) with open set W_i. Choose i₀ with Λ/(i + 1) < r/3 for i ≥ i₀. For i ≥ i₀, O_i := {x : dist(F_i x, y) > r/3} is open and contains spt X (dist(F_i x, y) ≥ dist(F x, y) − ‖F_i x − F x‖ > r − r/3). For x ∈ O_i, F_i x ∉ closedBall(y, r/3) ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(F_i x) = 0 and F_i^#ω(x) = 0; thus η_i = 0 on O_i ∩ W_i ⊇ spt X and X(η_i) = X(0) = 0 by (LOC). By (PA), lpush(F, X)(ω) = 0. So lpush(F, X) vanishes on B, B ⊆ zeroRegion(lpush(F, X)), and y ∉ spt lpush(F, X). Hence spt lpush(F, X) ⊆ F(spt X).
10. Conjunct (5). X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} with compact support, M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞ is NC (boundaryMassOn X univ = M(∂X)), and ∂X is NC by (iv). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}), F_i := Mo(F, Λ), and η_i := CP(F_i, ω, spt X) with open W_i ⊇ spt X ⊇ spt ∂X, on which η_i = F_i^#ω and dη_i = F_i^#(dω). By (PA) for ∂X and η_i: lpush(F, ∂X)(ω) = lim ∂X(η_i) = lim X(dη_i). By (PA) for X, the form dω and the forms dη_i (valid since dη_i = F_i^#(dω) on W_i): lpush(F, X)(dω) = lim X(dη_i). Since ∂lpush(F, X)(ω) = lpush(F, X)(dω), ext gives (5).
11. Conjunct (6). Take F_j := Mo(F, Λ): C^∞, Λ-Lipschitz, and sup_x ‖F_j x − F x‖ ≤ Λ/(j + 1) → 0, i.e. TendstoUniformly F_j F. Given ω, let η_j := CP(F_j, ω, spt X) together with its open set W_j ⊇ spt X on which η_j = F_j^#ω. By (PA) (‖DF_j‖ ≤ Λ; uniform convergence on ℝ^N implies it on spt X), X(η_j) → lpush(F, X)(ω). □
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: test forms have finite sup norms of ω and dω; spt X = ∅ ⇒ X = 0; NC is closed under differences and boundaries.
Comparison: the sibling estimate (E) bounds |X(η'') − X(η')| by sup_{spt X}|F' − G'| times C_X(Λ'', ω).
Definition: lpush(F, X)(ω) := lim X(η_i^ω) for mollified F_i and cut-off pull-backs; Cauchy by (E), linear by (LOC), bounded by (L1)+(MSB); a current by (BC); 0 otherwise.
(PA): any smooth approximants with derivative bounds on spt X give the same limit, by (E) against the defining sequence.

Conjuncts (1)–(6) follow from (PA) with suitable approximants (id; a common cut-off for spt X ∪ spt Y; the same mollifiers for F and G; mass by (L1)+(MSB); support by moving F_i(spt X) away from tsupport ω; boundary via dη_i = F_i^#dω; mollifiers for (6)).

Comparison with arbitrary smooth approximants proves the exact PA interface. PA then establishes all six parent conjuncts, with normality of differences and boundaries explicitly justified.
